title: Power Plant — Installation of Bushings in the Forward Engine Mount Bolt Bores
abstract: Installation of a shrink-fitted steel bushing in each forward engine mount bolt bore, giving a renewable wear surface and turning a future fretting finding into a bushing change rather than a fitting change.

sections.planning_reason: Fretting marks and light bore ovality have been reported at the forward mount bolt positions on twelve CVX-7200 powered aircraft, the earliest at 21 400 flight cycles. The bores are in a life limited fitting that cannot be reworked in service beyond a shallow polish, so a finding past the polish limit means a pylon fitting change and a long downtime. The bushing gives a sacrificial surface that is changed at the next engine removal instead.
sections.description: A steel bushing is shrink-fitted into each forward mount bolt bore. The upper bracket D7120112225413 is machined to the bushing interference fit and the forward bracket assembly D7120112258453 is exchanged for an item with the rework already applied. Titanium bolts LN569360-2A are retained at the mount, and tension bolts AES840808-93 secure the revised heat shield bracket FAR360439-80, which replaces the obsolete upper heat shield CAD50991-63.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the engine to the standard engine change procedure and support the pylon. Remove the pylon fairing panels to get access to the forward mount. Remove the titanium bolts LN569360-2A and the obsolete heat shield CAD50991-63. Do a detailed visual and eddy current inspection of each bolt bore and record the fretting depth and the ovality. Where a bore is outside the reworkable limit, stop and refer to Aeralis. Machine each bore to the bushing interference fit using the portable tool, working to the dimensions on the drawing. Cool the bushings and install them, then check the bore diameter after installation. Exchange the forward bracket assembly D7120112258453 for the reworked item and machine the upper bracket D7120112225413 in place. Install the heat shield bracket FAR360439-80 with tension bolts AES840808-93. Install the titanium bolts LN569360-2A and torque to the values given. Refit the pylon fairing panels and install the engine. Do the engine mount alignment check and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to TTN-88E1 aircraft with the CVX-7200 installation only. The Auran installation has a different mount geometry at the forward position and is not affected. Accomplishment is at a scheduled engine removal; this Service Bulletin does not justify an engine removal on its own.
sections.material_note: Kit K7120-1013-01 covers one pylon and contains the bushings, the reworked bracket assembly, the heat shield bracket and the fastener set. Kit lead time is twenty-six weeks. Bushings are also stocked individually for replacement at subsequent engine removals.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next engine removal after 20 000 flight cycles, or within 96 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
